status.wrongSecret: wrong secret: check the shared secret on both computers
status.versionMismatch: incompatible versions ({here} here, {there} on “{name}”): install the same version on both computers
status.sameRole: both computers are set as the {role} computer: one must be the main computer, the other the controlled one
status.unexpectedReply: unexpected reply from the other computer
status.captureFailed: cannot capture the keyboard and mouse: check the permissions

common.copyFailed: Cannot copy: select the text and copy it by hand.

layout.offlineText: This page appears as soon as Bascule is running.
layout.restartingWith: Bascule is restarting with the new settings…

actions.savedNoRestart: Settings saved, but Bascule did not restart.

home.waitingHelp: Make sure Bascule is running on the other computer, with the same secret.

settings.welcomeStep1: Choose this computer's role. The main computer is the one with the keyboard and mouse.
settings.welcomeStep2: The secret must be the same on both computers: copy this one into the other computer's settings, or paste its secret here.
settings.welcomeStep3: On the main computer, enter the other computer's address in “Connect to”. The other computer leaves this field empty.
settings.welcomeEnd: Save: Bascule restarts with these settings.
settings.configUnreadable: The configuration file cannot be read

machine.title: This computer
machine.primaryDesc: The keyboard and mouse are plugged into this computer (usually the PC).
machine.secondaryDesc: This computer is controlled from the other one (usually the Mac).
machine.name: Display name
machine.nameHelp: Optional. Defaults to the computer's name.

connection.intro: One computer waits for the connection, the other connects to it. Recommended: the Mac waits, the PC connects.
connection.addressHelp: Enter it in “Connect to” on the other computer.
connection.connectHelp: IP address (or .local name) of the other computer. Empty: this computer waits for the connection.
connection.secretHelp: Same on both computers (at least 12 characters).
connection.newSecretWarning: The new secret must also be copied to the other computer.
connection.listenHelp: Used when “Connect to” is empty. Rarely needs changing.
connection.activityHelp: This computer stays active while you are active on the other one: no display sleep or screen saver, “active” status in Teams, Discord… When you step away, it notices too. Turn it on on both computers.

switching.goToSecondaryHelp: The cursor comes back where it was.
switching.returnHereHelp: The same shortcut as above lets you go back and forth.
switching.hotkeysNeeded: Without edge switching, these two shortcuts are required.
switching.edgesHelp: Pushing the mouse against the edge moves to the other computer.
switching.positionHelp: Where the controlled computer's screen is, relative to this one.
switching.cornersHelp: In the corners, the edge does not switch computers (a window's ✕ button…). 0 = none.
switching.lockHelp: Locks or unlocks the cursor on the screen where it is.

mouse.scrollingHelp: By line, like a Windows mouse wheel; by pixel, more precise; smooth, animated and accelerated like Mac Mouse Fix (macOS).
mouse.smoothSpeedHelp: Distance per notch; notches close together go further.
mouse.smoothnessHelp: How long scrolling glides after each notch. Same settings as Mac Mouse Fix.
mouse.precisionHelp: A single notch scrolls only 10 pixels; quick notches still accelerate (Mac Mouse Fix option).
mouse.trackpadHelp: Scrolling is sent as a trackpad gesture followed by its momentum: bounce at the end of pages, momentum handled by apps… (Mac Mouse Fix option).
mouse.sideButtonsHelp: Buttons for Chrome, Firefox, VS Code… “Swipe” gesture for Safari, Finder, Xcode…

keyboard.mediaKeysHelp: Volume, playback…: on the computer where the cursor is, or always on one of the two computers.

clipboard.sensitiveHelp: Passwords copied from a password manager.

interface.trayIconHelp: Icon in the menu bar or notification area. Monochrome: matches the other system icons.

advanced.isoSwapHelp: European (ISO) Mac keyboards swap these two keys compared to a PC keyboard. “Auto” corrects this based on the Mac's keyboard: only change it if they stay swapped.
advanced.commandsHelp: For other apps (Keyboard Maestro, Shortcuts, AutoHotkey…): the keyboard and mouse move to this computer (here), to the other one (other) or to the one they are not on (toggle). “status” shows Bascule's state. “Copy” gives the full command, with Bascule's path:

settings.linuxNotice: On Linux, Bascule does not share the keyboard and mouse yet: these settings have no effect here.

about.tagline: One keyboard, one mouse and a shared clipboard between a PC and a Mac.
about.thanksText: Built with Rust, Tauri, Vue and Naive UI. Smooth scrolling follows the algorithm of Mac Mouse Fix, by Noah Nuebling.
